advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Update reconcile_check's module docstring to note that the `backend=None` default resolves the backend via `select_backend(load_config())` (config/env read), so purity holds only when a backend is injected.
evidence: reconcile_check.py:8: `The function :func:`reconcile_check` is pure (no I/O besides the return`
reconcile_check.py:292-296: `if backend is None:` then `from rebar.config import load_config` / `backend = select_backend(load_config())`
`load_config` resolves in the installed environment (rebar/config.py) and performs config file/env resolution (I/O)
advisory.finding: The module docstring still asserts `reconcile_check` is pure ('no I/O besides the return value'), but the new `backend is None` default path calls `select_backend(load_config())`, which reads config from disk/env and constructs an AcliClient transport — so the top-of-file purity claim is now inaccurate for the default invocation.
advisory.suggested_fix: Amend the docstring to say the function is pure WHEN a backend is injected; the `backend=None` default lazily loads config to select the configured backend (mirroring the outbound differ).

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a reconcile_check test asserting a genuinely divergent local vs remote description reports exactly one `description` discrepancy (and, ideally, that an oversized-but-normalized body does NOT read as drift).
evidence: reconcile_check.py:180-189 rewrites the description branch to `backend.outbound.map_fields_to_remote(...)` + `str(fitted or '').rstrip() == str(canonical.get('description') or '').rstrip()`

search for `"field": "description"` and `field == "description"` in tests/unit/rebar_reconciler returns only conftest.py:134 (a different suite's fixture) — no reconcile_check description-drift assertion

ABSENCE: every reconcile_check description input pairs local 'Hello' with ADF 'Hello' (test_reconcile_check_canonical.py:75/86, _live_binding, heldout _local/_base_jira); the only description-specific test (test_no_spurious_truncation_warning) asserts a log, not a discrepancy — the negative path (local≠remote description → one description discrepancy) is untested
advisory.finding: The rewritten description comparison branch (now backend.outbound.map_fields_to_remote fit + rstrip tolerance vs canonical.get('description')) has no test asserting a GENUINE description divergence produces a discrepancy. All description tests use matching text ('Hello'=='Hello') plus a no-warning assertion; a regression that made the description branch always report matches would pass every existing test.
scenarios: backend.outbound.map_fields_to_remote returns wrong/empty output so real description drift is silently suppressed
the ADF-fit tolerance for an oversized body is inverted and drops actionable drift
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a test: local description 'Hello' vs remote ADF 'Goodbye' → assert exactly one discrepancy with field=='description'; plus an oversized-description case asserting in_sync via the ADF-fit tolerance.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a reconcile_check test where the local assignee matches NONE of the canonical assignee_identity forms and assert exactly one `assignee` discrepancy is reported.
evidence: reconcile_check.py:171-179 new call `_assignee_matches(str(local_val or ''), canonical.get('assignee'), canonical.get('assignee_identity'))`
test_reconcile_check_canonical_heldout.py:93-98 parametrizes `local_assignee` over ['acc-1','User X','user@x.com'] and asserts `[d ... if d['field']=='assignee'] == []` (all matching cases)
ABSENCE: no reconcile_check test supplies a local assignee that does NOT match any canonical identity form and asserts an `assignee` discrepancy is produced
advisory.finding: The rewritten assignee branch uses the new 3-argument _assignee_matches(local, canonical.get('assignee'), canonical.get('assignee_identity')) but only the MATCHING path is tested (identity forms acc-1/User X/user@x.com all → in_sync). No test asserts that a genuinely divergent assignee yields an assignee discrepancy, so a regression making assignee always-match would pass every assignee test.
scenarios: _assignee_matches or the assignee_identity plumbing regresses to always-True, silently hiding a real assignee mismatch
canonical.get('assignee_identity') returns an unexpected shape and the negative branch misbehaves
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a heldout case: local assignee 'someone-else@y.com' against _base_jira() assignee (acc-1/User X/user@x.com) → assert one discrepancy with field=='assignee'.
